newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 23.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Wednesday:
* Philippine shares are seen locked within a narrow band as investors await the release of first half company earnings and further developments in the financial markets.

* "Focus is expected to again shift to corporate results which should start trickling in by this week. We continue to expect results to be mixed, likely with more bad than good," said Spencer Yap, analyst at BPI Securities Corp.
* Sun Hung Kai Securities said the main index will likely move within the 2,600 to 2,750 range.
* On Tuesday, the Philippine composite index closed slightly higher by 8.39 points at 2,656.73 points.
* The Dow Jones on Tuesday ended 154.93 points higher at 8,061.65. PLDT's ADR closed up $0.01 at $33.07.
* The Philippine peso ended lower at 28.15 to a dollar vs 28.0. Trading was range-bound and quiet as banks concentrated on meeting commercial requirements of clients, traders said.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was at 25.0625 percent vs 25.09375 percent.
* Petron Corp said its net income in the first half of the year jumped 13 percent to 2.25 billion pesos and analysts said the figure was expected despite stiffer competition.

* Pilipino Telephone Corp president Ramon Cojuangco told Reuters the company will launch a marketing offensive after it has shielded its network from cloning. "Slowly we are recovering. Judge us in the fourth quarter," he said.

* PLDT said it expected to lose two billion pesos this year if international rates were cut by 10 percent and government failed to approve its proposed new rate plan that will involve a rate hike for basic phone charges and a call metering scheme.

* The Philippines is expected to report stronger gross national product (GNP) growth in the second quarter compared with the 6.1 percent posted in the first quarter, Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito told Reuters.

* The Philippine central bank has barred onshore banks from selling non-deliverable forward (NDF) dollars to offshore counterparties for the next three months to allow the central bank to review the legality and practice of the derivative instrument.

* Filinvest Land Inc said it had paid a fine of 123,500 pesos imposed by the Securities and Exchange Commission for alleged late disclosure of a cease-and-desist order issued for its Sky City leisure estate project.

* Manila Electric Co (Meralco) president Manuel Lopez kilowatt-hour sales rose six percent in the first half of the year but were a little below target. Meralco's board has approved a 1.50 peso cash dividend.
* Ayala Land Inc has bought 76 million shares of Cebu Property Ventures and Development Corp from the Cebu provincial government for a total of 144 million pesos, Cebu Property said.

* Newspaper BusinessWorld said the central bank intends to invest the proceeds of the country's $715 million loan from the International Monetary Fund in interest-earning dollar instruments to recover its cost of using the funds.

* The Manila Bulletin said the country's gross international reserves (GIR) is expected to improve by about 7.34 percent to $10.45 billion from $9.7 billion with the disbursement today of financing facility from the IMF.

* The Philippine Star said an agriculture expert warned of a rice shortage due to a drought caused by the El Nino phenomenon and recommended the imporation of up to 950,000 tonnes of rice to ensure adequate supply until next year.
